metaData.originalTitle: MiniMax M3 一手实测：老黄 PPT 上 74 个 Logo，我以为能难住它
metaData.title: MiniMax M3 Hands-On Test: I Thought 74 Logos on Jensen Huang's PPT Would Stump It
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Through hands-on tests including reproducing a paper, identifying PPT logos, creating a check-in map, and explaining a linguistics olympiad video, this article validates MiniMax M3's comprehensive performance in long context, multimodality, and coding, concluding that it has entered the global first tier.
metaData.summary: The article focuses on MiniMax's latest open-source flagship model, M3, evaluating its three core capabilities: long context, multimodality, and coding. The author designed four hands-on tasks: independently reproducing an ICLR 2025 award-winning paper (12 hours without human intervention), identifying the 74 DSX ecosystem enterprise logos from Jensen Huang's Computex keynote PPT and creating an interactive webpage, making a food check-in map based on Jensen Huang's Beijing itinerary, and understanding a linguistics olympiad explanation video to reproduce a problem-solving webpage. All tasks were completed successfully, demonstrating M3's comprehensive abilities in long-form autonomous programming, multimodal understanding, information retrieval, and webpage generation. The article also introduces key technologies behind M3: the MSA sparse attention mechanism (reducing per-token computation to 1/20th of the previous generation at 1M context), an interactive user simulator framework (used for training coding and agent capabilities), and a native multimodal approach that mixes text and images from the first step of pre-training. Finally, the article points out that M3 is the first open-source model to simultaneously possess these three capabilities, with comprehensive performance approaching top-tier closed-source models like Claude Opus and GPT-5.5, offering outstanding cost-effectiveness.

mainPoints.point: M3 achieves top-tier performance in long context, multimodality, and coding simultaneously, a first for an open-source model.
mainPoints.explanation: Previously, only closed-source flagships like Claude Opus, GPT-5.5, and Gemini 3.1 could handle all three tasks. M3 is the first open-source model to break through this barrier, scoring 59% on SWE-Bench Pro, surpassing GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro.

mainPoints.point: Hands-on tasks validated M3's reliability in complex, long-form autonomous programming.
mainPoints.explanation: When reproducing the ICLR 2025 award-winning paper, M3 operated autonomously for 12 hours, producing 18 commits and 23 experimental charts. It diagnosed and adjusted issues independently without any human intervention, demonstrating autonomy close to that of a human research assistant.

mainPoints.point: M3's multimodal capabilities cover text, images, and video, enabling cross-modal synergy.
mainPoints.explanation: From identifying 74 logos in a PPT to understanding a nearly 2-hour linguistics olympiad video and reproducing a problem-solving webpage, M3 demonstrates a complete closed loop from visual input to code output. Its native multimodal approach (mixing text and images from the first step of pre-training) is key.

mainPoints.point: The MSA sparse attention mechanism and interactive user simulator are M3's core technical highlights.
mainPoints.explanation: MSA uses KV blocks to aggregate queries for the outer loop, achieving efficient hardware utilization and reducing per-token computation to 1/20th of the previous generation at 1M context. The interactive user simulator exposes the model to collaboration scenarios close to production environments during training, enhancing coding and agent capabilities.

keyQuotes: M3 is the first domestic open-source model to simultaneously achieve these three things (long context, multimodality, and coding).
This image itself is the best proof of reproduction, showing that M3 independently followed the same derivation path as the paper's authors and arrived at the same answer.

Frontier model capabilities have long been controlled by a few closed-source products, a situation that has hardly been broken in the past few years... M3 is the first open-source model to tear open this gap.

relatedArticles.title: Claude Mythos Officially Announced! Outperforming Opus 4.6, Held Back Due to 'Extreme Danger'
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic has unveiled the preview version of its next-generation model, Claude Mythos, which significantly outperforms Opus 4.6; however, due to its formidable cyberattack capabilities, the company has restricted public access under 'Project Glasswing' to bolster industry-wide security defenses.

relatedArticles.title: AI R&D Automation: Wiki Knowledge Base + Skill Pack
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to build a continuously growing team knowledge base and a supporting expert skill pack based on the LLM-Wiki model and the Obsidian platform to achieve AI-driven R&D automation.

relatedArticles.title: QuantumBit Exclusive Interview with Lou Tiancheng: AI is a Runaway Horse, and Harness is the Most Critical Skill of This Era
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Pony.ai CTO Lou Tiancheng elaborates on the core philosophy of the PonyWorld World Model 2.0: when AI driving capabilities surpass humans, the value of human data drops to zero, AI must become the 'head coach' leading R&D, and the ability to harness this 'runaway horse' of AI will be the most critical skill of this era.

relatedArticles.title: Google's New Paper Crashes Memory Stocks! 6x KV Cache Compression, Netizens: Silicon Valley Becomes Reality
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Google Research releases the TurboQuant algorithm, achieving at least 6x lossless compression of the KV cache via techniques like polar quantization, significantly reducing memory requirements for LLM inference and boosting speed.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: Can AI Write Code in Truly "Mission-Critical" Backend Systems?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article shares the complete methodology—Harness Engineering—practiced by Tencent's CDN LEGO team for AI coding in ultra-large-scale, high-reliability backend systems. Through a five-layer architecture, three key levers (context, constraints, feedback), and multi-model adversarial code review, they built an engineering system that enables AI to safely and controllably produce high-quality code.

relatedArticles.title: The Second Half of Large Model Architecture
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article proposes that large model architecture has entered a second half centered on 'scaling communication,' critiques the traditional 'accumulation' paradigm of residual connections, and introduces innovative solutions for inter-layer 'selective retrieval' through Flash Depth Attention and MoDA.

relatedArticles.title: A Practical Guide to 'Progressive Spec' for AI Coding in 2026
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article proposes a 'Progressive Spec' framework for AI coding environments, leveraging structured documentation to drive AI collaboration and balance development standards with execution efficiency.

relatedArticles.title: The Evolution of Agent/Skills/Teams Architectures and Principles of Technology Selection
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically reviews the evolutionary trajectory of AI Agents from monolithic to multi-agent, then to Skills pluginization and Teams parallel collaboration, and, drawing on the latest research from Google and Anthropic, provides a scientific methodology for selection.

relatedArticles.title: DeepSeek V4 Report Is Incredibly Detailed! The Full Story of the 484-Day Upgrade Journey
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: DeepSeek officially released the V4 series of models, achieving a KV cache of only 10% of V3.2 under a million-token context through the mHC architecture, hybrid attention mechanism, and Muon optimizer, while being fully open-source and supporting domestic chips.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: How I Spent a Week Boosting AI Coding Rate to 90% in an Enterprise App
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces Harness Engineering, a new AI coding paradigm that elevates the AI code rate of an enterprise Java application from 25% to over 90% by building a four-element system of rules, skills, knowledge, and change management.
